rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS FROM GRADE 10 TO GRADE 18 AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: It has been found by the Congresssional Commission on Education that teacher's complaints center on three principal problems: namely, low salaries, too many activities that are not related to teaching, and non-implementat ion of existinglaws granting benefits to teachers.  The cornerstone of any public policy to upgrade teachers' quality must be the restoration of their dignity and their standard of living.  The initial step to restore the image off the teaching profession is to uplift the economic condition of the teachers. To achieve this, it is imperative that their salaries should be upgraded to that level where they could live a decent and respective life.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 1997-04-23

rows.abstract: Rationale: As the country prepares its human resource for active participation in the fulfillment of national development goals, it is a must that the very people who carry out this vital mission be equally prepared for the job. Incentives must be offered in order to attract the best maids to enter the teaching profession and make teaching competitive.> This bill is an attempt not only to improve the ploght of teachers but also to encourage qualified individuals to enter the teching profession.Hence, its approval is urgently and earnestly recommended. rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING DRUG TEST FOR CERTAIN APPLICATIONS, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR FRAUDULENT ACTS RELATIVE THERETO AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Drug addiction is considered as one of the evils of today's Filipino society.  The government is trying to combat this epidemic, but the task of preventing drug abuse remains a challenge to all sectors of society. Thousands of people of all ages are subjecting themselves to the harmful influences of drugs which they do so out of curiosity, for pleasure, or in order to deal with stressful events or painful experiences. More often the use of these prohibited drugs leads to the commission of other crimes. Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. Applicants for the following shall, upon filing of their application, be required to udnergo drug test under the supervision of the Department of Health: (1) driver's license; (2) licensee for the possession of firearms and other deadly weapons; (3) security guard license; (4) government licensure examinations; (5) employment in government and government owned and controlled corporations whether as casual, contractual or permanent po
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-04-28

rows.author: A027
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO BARANGAY OFFICIALS, BY AMENDING SECTION 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Considering the amount of responsibility and extent of public service placed by the barangay officials in the performance of their official duty, it is very sad to note that the law fails to provide them assurance that their future will be taken care of by the State. Currently, the barangay officials are not enjoying retirement benefits that would at least see them through after their separation from the public service. Proposes the following for our barangay officials --- "(6) BE ENTITLED TO RETIREMENT BENEFITS AFTER THEIR SEPARATION FROM THE PUBLIC SERVICE. PROVIDED, THAT THE BENEFITS UNDER THIS PROVISION SHALL BE AVAILED OF ONLY BY ELECTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE RENDERED PUBLIC SERVICE FOR AT LEAST THREE TERMS, WHETHERCONSECUTIVE OR NOT. PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE RENDERED SERVICE FOR AT LEAST TEN YEARS, WHETHER CONTINUOUS  OR NOT, ARE ALSO ENTITLED TO THE BENEFITS OF THIS ACT."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-04-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING PASSAGE OF PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION VEHICLES THROUGH PRIVATE STREETS AND THOROUGHFARES BY MANDATING THE OPENING OF PRIVATE SUBDIVISIONS AND VILLAGES ON PEAK HOURS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: This legislative measure seeks to remedy traffic problem  in the metropolis. However, by trying to do so it needs to resort to the exercise of the State's police power. Although the Constitution guarantees certain areas of a persons's property which the government cannot touch, still the legislature is vested with police powers to "[m]ake, ordain and establish all manners of wholesome and reasonable laws, statutes, and ordinances, either with penalties or without, not repugnant to the Constitution, as they shall judge to be for the good and welfare of the commonwealth, and of the subjects of the same. States, therefore, for the following --- "SECTION 1. For the de-congestion of traffic in main roads and highways, all streets andd thoroughfares of private subdivisions and vilalges shall be opened on peak hours to allow the passage of public transporation vehicles. Provided, however, a maxium of fours hours shall be the duration for allowing the passage of PUJs/PUVs through t
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-04-28

rows.author: A027
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF THE HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENC Y VIRUS (HIV) AND ACQUIRED IMMUNITY DEFICIENCY SYNDROME (AIDS) BY REQUIRING AN 'AIDS CLEARANCE CERTIFICATE' (ACC) FROM SEX WORKERS, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONSTHEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The government has formulated the AIDS Prevention and Control Program under the DOH and has implemented the "Stop-AIDS" information campaign, among others, to promote people's awareness and to understand AIDS for its prevention. Moreover,existing laws require sex workers to seek health clearances and working permits from local government. Unfortunately, reports even revealed majority of sex entertainers are working with the necessary license. Thus, AIDS continue to pose a threat topublic health.  Given all these, it becomes necessary to strenghten the power and widen the manpower of the Department of Health to ensure that the spread of AIDS is minimized. "AIDS Control Act of 1997" Provides for the creation of an HIV/AIDS ACC (( Aids Clearance Certificate) DIVISION in the Dept. of Health which shall conduct checkup and physcial examination of sex workers and to issue or cancel the ACC. Provides. likewise, for the requirements of issuance of the ACC.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-04-28

rows.author: A053
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING WEDDING ANNIVERSARY LEAVE OF ONE (1) DAY WITH FULL PAY TO EVERY LEGALLY MARRIED EMPLOYEES IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This proposed Bill aims to uphold the mandate of the constitution that marriage is an inviolable social institution and the foundation of the family. The State recognized the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation. "Wedding Anniversary Leave Act of 1997"  Applies to those who are legally married; excludes those marriages have been severed by legal separation and by an order of annulment. Wedding shall include civil or chuch wedding.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR A PROGRAM OF MODERNIZATION FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The current bill is intended to be a companion measure to the revised University Charter.  It draws from the vision of UP Plan 2008, the University's strategic plan up ot is first centennial and into the twenty-first century.  The UP Modernization Program seeks to provide Congressional support and resources to major areas which the University must develop to keep its lead in and provide support for the Philippine educational system, assure its place in the international system of universities, and enhance its capacity to respond to the major problems of our national life. Prescribes the following components of the Program: (1() Development of More Comprehensive Autonomous Campuses; (2) Expansion of Centers of Excellence; (3) Creeation of Complexes; (4) Expansion and Development of Learning and Resource Centers; (5) Modernization of the Philippine General Hospital; and (6) Administrative System and Governance.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Seagrass are a rich breeding and feeding grounds for small fishes, shells, and other animal marine life. They are creeping underwater plants near shores that, unlike seaweeds, produce flowers and fruits. > If corals are fish breeding grounds, seagrass are their nurseries and playgrounds. During low tide, a variety of mullusks, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, crustaceans, ells, mussels, snails, small fish and shellfish can be picked from seagrass beds by fishermen and even birds. > Seeksto INCLUDE, "SEAGRASSES" as among the aquatic resources (ordering corals included) mandated by law to be protected and conserved, their use of which is considered a PUNISHABLE act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING CHILD AND FAMILY COURTS, GRANTING THEM EXCLUSIVE ORIGINAL JURISDICTION OVER CHILD AND FAMILY CASES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  As a signatory to the UN convention to the Rights of the Child, our country through this bill further aims to correct the glaring and obvious discrepancies in ineffectively handling  of youth offender cases by our present judicial system.  Our non-compliance to the UN minimum standard, to the provisions of the convention, to the UN committee on Children as required by the UN Beijing rules has been cited in the Geneva convention of January 1995. "Child and Family Courts Act  of 1997"Places the following cases under the  EXCLUSIVE ORIGINAL JURISDICTION of the child and Family Courts: (1) criminal cases where the accused is below  18 years of age at the  time of the office; (2) petitions for guardianship, custody of children, ?in relation to the latter; (3) petition for the adoption of children; (4) complaints for the annulment of marriage, declaration of nullity of marriage, etc; (5) petitions for support, etc.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING AN ANTI-KIDNAPPING AND -BANK ROBBERY  UNIT UNDER THE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION GROUP OF THE PNP, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 35(b) (4) OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED SEVENTY-FIVE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The recent spate of kidnapping and bank robberies continue to haunt the country. Despite the eforts of the Philippine National Police, the number of reported kidnappings continue to escalate thus earning us the monicker "the Kidnap Capital of Asia", as one international magazine recently reported. Mandates the creation of a SPECIAL ANTI-KIDNAPPING AND-BANK ROBBERY UNIT which shall serve as a primary reaction term to undertake the (1) monitoring; (2) investigation; and (3) prosecutionof all kidnapping and bank robbery gangs and cases in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 1997-04-30

rows.abstract: Rationale: Seeks to STRENGTHEN the SK organization in the midst of criticisms hurled against them, especially after the May 1996 election, which was reportedly marred with irregularities , which were not, in any way of SK's own doing. These amendatory provisions seek to --- (1) allocate MORE FUNDS to the SK organizations and their officials; (2) grant MORE POWER to the SK officials, particularly in the management of their affairs; (3) REINFORCE the processes and procedures of its operations where the SK officials become primarily responsible.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-04-30

rows.author: A100
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAXIMUM USE OF PHILIPPINE FLAG VESSELS AND AIR CARRIERS, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED EIGHT HUNDRED AND NINETY-FOUR, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED 'REQUIRING GOVERNMENT OFFICES, AGENCIES, INSTRUMENTALITI ES AND GOVERNMENT-OWNE D OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, PERSONS AND ENTITIES ENJOYING TAX EXEMPTION, INCENTIVES OR SUBSIDY FROM THE GOVERNMENT TO UTILIZE IN INTERNATIONAL TRANSPORTATION THE SERVICES OF THE PHILIPPINE FLAG AIR CARRIER AND SHIPPING LINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale:  As an island nation, the Philippines is dependent upon air and sea transport for all foreign trade. Currently, the vast majority of imports and exports are carried by non-Filipino companies with vital markets such as Europe, the Middle East, Australia, and South America. The Philippines is entirely dependent upon foreign ocean and air carriers for the movements of Filipino exports. Transport freight revenue loses incurred by the Philippines is in the billions of pesos, leaving the Filipinos at the mercy of foreign lines when it comes to the economic security of their nation. Seeks to ensure that ALL "taxpayer-suppo rted" cargo imports are FIRST OFFERED to Philippine companies, thereby (1) ensuring the stability to the Philippinnes of an ocean and air carrier fleet,a s well as (2) securing a training ground for Filipino seaman and pilots.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1997-04-30

rows.author: A100
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE AMUSEMENT TAX ON GROSS RECEIPTS FROM ADMISSION FEES OF THEATERS AND CINEMAS FROM THIRTY(30%) TO TEN PERCENT(10%), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: For a few pesos, moviegoers tend to forget their worries even for a few hours and had themselves immersed in the loftiness or inanities of foreign or local movies. It is, therefore, only fair and just that we give due recognition and/or incentives to filmmakers to encourage them to produce more meaningful movies.  This bill is a step in this direction.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING THE ISSUANCE OF FIREARM LICENSES DURING ELECTION PERIOD, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 32 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 1991 SYNCHRONIZED ELECTION LAW
rows.abstract: Rationale: What is necessary to be prohibited for security purposes is the carrying of firearms, which would not include possessing, and more, the issuance, of firearm license during the election period.  To prohbit the possession and issuance of firearms license during election period, which usually runs for six (6) months before and after the election, effectively deprives duly licensed firearm dealers from doing their legitimate business during the period which is contrary to the state policy of encouraging private enterprise. > This bill seeks to lift the prohibition/sus pension of the issuance of firearm license during election period.
